gaps.explanation: Statement lines are the accrual Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Net Position - Proprietary Funds, Totals 2023 (pp9-10, printed pp14-15): Charges for services 549,463 + Lease agreement 241,234 + Miscellaneous 31,967 = Total operating revenues 822,664, + Interest revenue 65,286 = 887,950. The only business-type schedule is Schedule 29 'Statement of Cash Receipts and Cash Disbursements Compared to Budget' (p35, printed p69), Actual Budgetary Basis receipts: Electric 314,364 + Water 323,433 + Sewer 260,876 = 898,673 (detail lines, read correctly). Per fund: Electric 314,364 vs accrual 277,639 + 57,916 = 335,555; Water 323,433 vs 301,788 + 4,823 = 306,611; Sewer 260,876 vs 243,237 + 2,547 = 245,784. The budgetary receipts are cash-basis and include cash items outside accrual revenue (e.g. Proceeds of long-term debt 15,000 Water and 15,000 Sewer on the p11 cash flow statement); the accrual statement includes accrued interest/receivable changes. Schedule above by 10,723 because of the basis; no line missing or doubled.

Statement (pp9-10, accrual Totals 2023): Production and purchased power 50,761 + Maintenance and operation 189,906 + General 8,156 + Administrative 39,673 + Depreciation 238,769 + Interest expense 8,740 = 536,005. Schedule 29 (p35) Actual Budgetary Basis disbursements: Electric 163,632 + Water 314,482 + Sewer 265,951 = 744,065 (detail, one printed line per fund). The statement includes non-cash depreciation 238,769; the budgetary schedule includes cash outlays the accrual statement capitalizes or carries on the balance sheet (p11: purchase of capital assets 439,269 = Water 314,610 + Sewer 124,659; principal paid 24,341; interfund due to/from). Per fund: Electric 163,632 vs 88,916 (all depreciation); Water 314,482 vs 218,021; Sewer 265,951 vs 220,328 + 8,740 = 229,068. Printed totals 536,005 and 744,065 genuinely differ by basis (schedule above by 208,060); the one-line-per-fund schedule cannot be reconciled further.
